subtopics.title: Tilted Strata, Dip Slopes and Scarp Slopes

questions.question: Strata are never deposited on a slant; they become tilted when:
options: Crustal forces act on them — folding by plate collision, unequal uplift, or the sagging of loaded basins
Rain compacts one side of the stack
Wind piles sediment unevenly
Rivers deposit them at an angle

questions.question: The DIP of a tilted layer is defined as:
options: The depth of the layer below sea level
The angle the layer makes with the horizontal
The width of the ridge it forms
The compass bearing of the crest line

questions.question: Walking down a dip slope, the ground beneath your boots is:
options: A different layer every few steps
Loose river gravel
The SAME resistant layer's upper surface the entire way, at the angle of the dip
Always soft shale

questions.question: The scarp slope stands steep, often cliffed at the crest, because it:
options: Follows one hard layer downhill
Faces away from the prevailing wind
Was smoothed by glaciers
Slices ACROSS the stack, and rapid erosion of the exposed weak layers undermines the resistant edge above them

questions.question: A cuesta is built where strata lean:
options: Gently, up to roughly 25 degrees — a long easy dip slope against a short steep scarp
At exactly 45 degrees
Beyond 60 degrees
Not at all

questions.question: The Magaliesberg between Pretoria and Rustenburg is the celebrated South African example of a:
options: Cuesta basin
HOMOCLINAL RIDGE — quartzite strata leaning steeply, between roughly 25 and 45 degrees
Basaltic plateau
Pediplain

questions.question: A hogsback loses the asymmetry of the other two ridges because:
options: Its rock is uniformly soft
It has two caps of dolerite
With the layers leaning beyond roughly 45 degrees, BOTH faces cut across the upturned strata at similar steep angles — the gentle ramp disappears
Rivers erode both sides equally by chance

questions.question: The trend that ties the classification together is:
options: Steeper dip makes the ridge wider and more lopsided
Dip angle has no effect on ridge form
Gentler dip always produces a hogsback
Steeper dip narrows the ridge and makes its two faces more EQUAL, until the asymmetry vanishes near vertical

questions.question: In a cuesta basin the concentric ridges are arranged with:
options: Dip slopes facing INWARD toward the centre and scarps facing OUTWARD, because every layer descends toward the middle
Dip slopes facing outward and scarps inward
Both slopes facing outward
No resistant ridges at all

questions.question: A borehole near the centre of a cuesta basin can overflow without a pump because:
options: Basins always contain surface lakes
Rain entering the tilted aquifer at the rim travels down the dip and gathers under PRESSURE beneath the basin floor — artesian water
The rock at the centre is waterproof
Wind pushes the water upward

questions.question: In a cuesta dome the scarp slopes face:
options: Outward, down the arch
Vertically upward
INWARD, confronting one another across the eroded core, because every layer descends away from the centre
Always toward the sea

questions.question: The Vredefort Dome south-west of Johannesburg is world-famous because:
options: It is an active volcano
It is the deepest canyon in Africa
It is built of horizontal lava flows
An ancient impact arched the strata and erosion has etched them into concentric rings of ridges — a World Heritage Site

subtopics.title: Reading Tilted Country on the Map

questions.question: The contour signature of a cuesta or homoclinal ridge is:
options: Contours packed hard against one side of the crest and strung wide apart on the other
Perfect circles around a central peak
Identical spacing on both flanks
No contours near the crest

questions.question: Crest at 900 m; the 750 m contour lies 300 m away to the east and 3 000 m away to the west. The gradients are:
options: East 1 in 20 and west 1 in 2
East 1 in 2 and west 1 in 20 — the east is the scarp and the strata dip westward
1 in 300 on both sides
East 1 in 3 and west 1 in 30

questions.question: A cross-section uses a vertical scale of 1 cm to 50 m against a 1:50 000 horizontal scale. The vertical exaggeration is:
options: 5 times
50 times
10 times — the vertical scale is 1:5 000, and 50 000 divided by 5 000 gives 10
2 times

questions.question: Human activity fits tilted country by placing:
options: Towns along the hogsback crests
Railways straight up the scarp faces
Dams on the dip-slope summits
Farms on the gentle dip slopes, towns and roads in the strike valleys, and crossings where rivers have sawn poorts through the crest — as at Olifantsnek in the Magaliesberg

questions.question: In the tilted-sandwich picture, the smooth top slice you run a finger down stands for:
options: The DIP SLOPE — a gentle ramp riding on one layer's surface all the way down
The scarp slope
The valley between two ridges
The crest of a hogsback

questions.question: The cut end of the sandwich, showing every layer's sawn-off edge, stands for:
options: The dip slope
The SCARP SLOPE — the steep face slicing across all the layers at once
An artesian aquifer
A pediment

questions.question: The memory line 'dip follows, scarp cuts' captures the fact that:
options: Both slopes ride on the same layer
The scarp is always the gentler face
The dip slope runs along ONE layer's surface while the scarp cuts across the edges of MANY layers
Dip slopes exist only in sandwiches

subtopics.title: Three Clicks of the Car Jack

questions.question: The three clicks of the jack, in order of increasing lean, produce:
options: Cuesta, homoclinal ridge, hogsback
Hogsback, homoclinal ridge, cuesta
Mesa, butte, conical hill
Cuesta, hogsback, homoclinal ridge

questions.question: The 'wheelbarrow ramp against a short steep cut end' describes click one, which is a:
options: Hogsback
CUESTA — strata leaning gently, up to about 25 degrees
Cuesta dome
Pediplain

questions.question: At click three, past about 45 degrees, the ramp disappears because:
options: The rock melts
The ridge sinks into the valley
With the layers standing nearly upright, BOTH faces cut across sawn-off edges and both are steep
The sandwich falls off the jack

questions.question: The Magaliesberg matches click two because it is:
options: A flat-lying basalt plateau
A ring of ridges around an impact site
A gently leaning cuesta you could plough
A quartzite ridge with strata leaning steeply between about 25 and 45 degrees, running over a hundred kilometres

subtopics.title: Dishes, Umbrellas and the Gap in the Ridge

questions.question: The satellite dish stands for a cuesta basin, in which:
options: Gentle dip slopes face INWARD toward the centre and the scarp rims face OUTWARD
Dip slopes face outward on every side
There are no concentric ridges
The strata lie perfectly flat

questions.question: The self-raising water under the middle of the dish is called:
options: Tidal water
ARTESIAN water — rim rainfall that slid down inside a tilted layer and sits under pressure beneath the centre
Meltwater
Capillary water

questions.question: The umbrella stands for:
options: A canyon
A homoclinal ridge
A CUESTA DOME — dip slopes facing outward down the arch, scarps facing inward across the gutted core, like the Vredefort Dome
A mesa

questions.question: The highway and the dam share the same breach at Olifantsnek because:
options: Engineers enjoy building beside dams
The ridge crest is the easiest place to cross
The valleys were too narrow for a road
Crossing a resistant ridge is only practical where a river has already sawn a poort through it — human routes obey the rock
